name: Felix
overview: Felix was a male figure known as the governor of Caesarea, as identified in Acts 23:24. Beyond his official role, there are no additional personal or tribal details recorded. His position as governor places him within the Roman administrative structure during the early Christian era.
namesAndTitles: The name 'Felix' appears as a proper name without a given meaning in the biblical record, simply identifying this individual. He is also referred to by the title 'Governor Felix,' which clarifies his official capacity and authority in Caesarea as noted in Acts 23:26.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Felix beyond his role as governor of Caesarea. There are no documented relatives or personal connections listed in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Felix's significance in the biblical narrative arises from his position as the Roman governor overseeing Caesarea, a key administrative center. His role would have involved judgment and governance during a formative period in the early church, as indicated by his mention in Acts. This highlights the intersection of Roman authority and the early Christian movement within the New Testament context.
